newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Owners of disabled drilling rig assess damage.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Owners of disabled drilling rig assess damage.

text.p: The owner-operator of an oil drilling rig disabled during installation in waters off South Australia was on Sunday assessing the cause and extent of damage, explorer Canyon (Australia) Pty Ltd said.

Canyon spokesman Chris Rann said officials from Maersk Drilling (Australia) Ltd APS, which owned and operated the 8,500 tonne Maersk Victory had arrived from Singapore to assess damage to the rig and options for its repair or removal.
Thirty five workers were evacuated on Saturday when one of the rig's legs was believed to have struck unstable bottom while being positioned in the Gulf St Vincent, south of Adelaide.

The 50 metre high rig was being positioned for a A$15 million offshore petroleum exploration program by Canyon, which Rann said was 100 percent owned by the private Texan based oil and gas explorer and producer Wagner and Brown Ltd.

Two wells were planned to target Cambrian age sediments of the Stansbury Basin. Rann said it was too early to speculate on the cause of damage or the delay in the drilling programme, but the company planned to begin drilling as soon as possible.
"Canyon and Wagner and Brown are committed to completing the exploration programme ...but its future will be determined by the availability of this or another rig," Rann said.
"There will probably be a better picture after Monday in terms of damage to the rig and what happens from here," he said.
